source.citation: Fukuchi RK, Fukuchi CA, Duarte M (2017). A public dataset of running biomechanics and the effects of running speed on lower extremity kinematics and kinetics. PeerJ 5:e3298
source.note: derived summary statistics from the raw marker and force files

method.axes: X = direction of travel (forward +), Y = vertical, Z = mediolateral; mm; markers 150 Hz, forces 300 Hz (Fy vertical, single plate under the treadmill). Sagittal plane = (X, Y).
method.events: foot strike / toe-off = first / last sample of Fy (5-sample median) above 20 N, linearly interpolated; contacts lasting 0.6-1.5 x the median contact; stride = strike to next strike of the same leg with alternating legs and step times within 30 % of the median
method.leg: contact assigned to the foot whose lowest marker (heel bottom, MT1, MT5) is lower over the middle 40 % of the contact
method.hip: gtr = greater trochanter reconstructed from the thigh marker cluster (static R.GTR / L.GTR carried by a rigid-body fit); hjc = Harrington 2007 pelvis regression on ASIS/PSIS (pelvis marker group fitted rigidly)
method.knee: lateral femoral epicondyle (static R.Knee) carried by the thigh-cluster fit
method.ankle: lateral malleolus (static R.Ankle) carried by the shank-cluster fit
method.forefoot: midpoint of MT1 and MT5 (a single one if the other is missing; the static angle is taken with the same choice)
method.filter: short gaps (<= 20 frames) interpolated; zero-lag 2nd-order Butterworth forward and backward, nominal 15 Hz; events by cubic interpolation
method.ground: per subject: median over all clean contacts of the lowest foot-marker height at mid-stance (marker height, not the belt surface)
method.kneeDeg: thighDeg - shankDeg (equals 180 deg minus the hip-knee-ankle included angle when the knee is flexed)
method.footDeg: heel-bottom to forefoot line above horizontal minus the same angle in the static trial (toe up positive)
method.swing: toe-off to next strike; stance: strike to toe-off
method.cohorts: legs averaged within subject; rearfoot = legs whose RFSI/LFSI value is "Rearfoot" (as tools/reduce-fukuchi.js)

method.note: added measurement: ground force line relative to the hip through the contact; the earlier fields of this file are unchanged
method.points: stance fractions 0, 5 ... 100 %; 0 and 100 % = the raw 20 N strike and toe-off; markers by cubic interpolation, forces by linear interpolation
method.filter: Fx, Fy and COPx of each contact are low-passed at 30 Hz (zero-lag 2nd-order Butterworth forward and backward, odd-reflection padding) for this block only; before filtering, COPx samples with Fy < 0.2 BW are replaced by the nearest valid value
method.mask: copAhead*, copAlongFoot, fxOverFy and lineAtHip* are NaN where Fy < 0.2 BW; stride, leg and subject means use the valid points only (ok_* = fraction of strides valid)
method.signs: forward +; Fx is the force on the runner (braking negative); copAhead* = COPx - x(point), m; copAlongFoot = copAheadHeel / standing heel-to-forefoot-marker distance (X, m; forefoot = MT1/MT5 midpoint)
method.lineAtHip: copAheadHip + (Fx/Fy) * hip height above the plate; hip height above the plate = the marker Y of the hip point (the plate is Y = 0), i.e. the marker hip height used elsewhere plus the subject marker-ground offset (about 35 mm)
method.hipVelocity: hipVx / hipVy: lab-frame velocity of the trochanter-marker hip point, m/s; hipVxStride = (x at next strike - x at strike) / stride time
method.impulses: brakeImpulse / propImpulse = integral of negative / positive Fx dt / body mass, m/s, 300 Hz samples over the contact
method.events: fxZeroPct = first upward zero crossing of Fx after its minimum; copZeroPct = first + to - crossing of copAheadHip (1 % grid, valid force only); heelOffPct = Heel.Bottom first 10 mm above its 40-60 % stance median; peakFyPct = time of the maximum Fy; all as % of stance
method.copInFoot: fraction of valid points at 20-60 % of stance with heel x - 30 mm <= COPx <= max(MT1, MT5) x + 30 mm
method.hyN: hy_* = hip height above the plate (m) at strike, lowest in stance, toe-off; hyN_* divided by subject height; suffix _hjc = pelvis-regression hip
